section_summary: This closing section documents the State Department’s late-1939 “moral embargo” on supplying Japan and the Soviet Union with aviation-gasoline technology, related materials, and blending agents, together with Japan’s formal protest that the policy violated commercial treaty rights. It records negotiations with American petroleum and engineering companies over existing contracts, the withdrawal or movement of engineers, and the legal and commercial consequences of compliance. The section also contains company reports on 1939 exports, Department acknowledgments and requests for continued reporting, and correspondence concerning congressional material on exports to China and Japan.

subfiles.title: Telegram no. 717 reporting Japan's proposed protest against the moral embargo
subfiles.about: Reports that the Japanese Foreign Office intended to protest the American moral embargo and asked that its withdrawal be recommended.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Foreign Office said the restrictions on aluminum, molybdenum, gasoline, and manufacturing processes infringed the commercial treaty and threatened current efforts to improve Japanese-American relations. It distinguished the new policy from earlier humanitarian restrictions on aircraft and munitions, warning that failure to protest could invite an indefinite expansion of embargoed goods. Grew declined to recommend withdrawal but warned that public knowledge of the dispute could produce an adverse reaction in Japan.

subfiles.title: Department reply concerning the December 15 and December 20 policy statements
subfiles.about: Directs the Embassy to the Department's published statements concerning the recent export policy.
subfiles.summary: The Department identifies Radio Bulletins 295 and 299 as containing its statements of December 15 and December 20. It also calls attention to the statements' treatment of gasoline as a commodity, although the final wording is partly obscured by the OCR.

subfiles.title: Telegram reporting presentation of the Japanese Ambassador's note
subfiles.about: Informs the Embassy that the Japanese Ambassador presented a note about American measures discouraging specified exports.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Ambassador called under instructions and presented a formal note concerning American steps to discourage exports to certain countries. The affected categories included aircraft, aircraft parts, materials essential to aircraft production, and technical information needed to manufacture high-quality aviation gasoline.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs memorandum recommending no action on Shelton's departure
subfiles.to: Department of State files / Division of Controls
subfiles.about: Recommends that the Department take no immediate action on Universal Oil Products Company's request concerning George E. Shelton.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum notes that the Department's aviation-gasoline technology policy had already appeared in its December 20 radio bulletin. It finds no apparent reason that George E. Shelton would need Embassy assistance to leave Japan and recommends an oral reply in that sense if the company renews its request.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of telephone conversation with H. J. Halle about Japanese requests
subfiles.about: Records Halle's account of a Japanese inquiry into the legal basis of the Department's aviation-gasoline restrictions and his request for assistance to Shelton.
subfiles.summary: Halle reported that a Japanese representative questioned whether Universal Oil Products Company's refusal to provide further aviation-gasoline information resulted from an American request or order and challenged the Government's legal authority. Halle replied by comparing that challenge with Japanese treatment of Americans in China. He said the company would continue its ordinary-gasoline plant contract in Manchukuo and again asked that the Tokyo Embassy be informed of the policy and assist George E. Shelton in leaving Japan; Green declined to commit the Department and doubted that Americans would have difficulty departing.

subfiles.title: Standard-Vacuum report of no 1939 blending-agent sales
subfiles.from: Kersey F. Coe, Standard-Vacuum Oil Company
subfiles.to: Department of State, attention Joseph C. Green
subfiles.about: Reports that Standard-Vacuum sold no blending agents to Japan or the Soviet Union during 1939.
subfiles.summary: Coe responds in connection with L. K. Blood's earlier correspondence with the Department. He states unequivocally that Standard-Vacuum Oil Company made no 1939 sales of blending agents to either Japan or the Soviet Union.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Standard-Vacuum's blending-agent report
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Standard-Vacuum's statement that it made no relevant 1939 sales.
subfiles.summary: Green thanks Coe for the company's December 28 report. He restates that Standard-Vacuum did not sell blending agents in 1939 for export to Japan or the Soviet Union.

subfiles.title: Despatch no. 397 requesting congressional and export-control documents
subfiles.from: Willys R. Peck, for the U.S. Ambassador at Chungking
subfiles.about: Requests documents on iron-and-steel scrap and arms exports to China and Japan that were unavailable in the Chungking office.
subfiles.summary: The Chungking Embassy office asks for the Senate subcommittee hearings on restricting iron-and-steel scrap exports and a Division of Controls statement on arms, ammunition, and implements of war sent to China and Japan. Peck notes that the materials may have reached the Peiping office, but a search found no copies at Chungking.

subfiles.title: Instruction no. 197 supplying hearings and explaining the obsolete neutrality statement
subfiles.about: Provides requested Senate materials and explains why the Department no longer uses its earlier statement on arms exports.
subfiles.summary: The Department encloses Parts 1 and 2 of Senate hearings on S. 2025 and S.J. Res. 180, along with S. 3037 concerning protection of the domestic iron and steel industry for national defense. It reports that S. 3037 and a similar House bill remain pending without scheduled hearings. The requested Division of Controls statement had been based on the Neutrality Act of 1937 and was discontinued after that law was superseded by the Neutrality Act of 1939.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of discussions with H. J. Halle on contracts and company engineers
subfiles.about: Records the December 18 telephone call and December 19 meeting with Universal Oil Products Company about implementing the aviation-gasoline technology policy.
subfiles.summary: Halle sought guidance on an engineer waiting in Genoa before proceeding to Germany and on three company employees in the Soviet Union, while the Department offered to transmit coded instructions through the Moscow Embassy. At the December 19 meeting, Halle, W. D. Whitney, and Stanley Wilson discussed the risk of damages and litigation if Soviet contracts were broken and pressed unsuccessfully for documents naming Japan and the Soviet Union separately. The parties arranged possible Embassy assistance and travel funds for engineers leaving the Soviet Union, while decisions about engineers in Japan were left to the company's judgment. Halle also requested that the Tokyo Ambassador be informed of the policy.

subfiles.title: Instruction no. 1872 transmitting aviation-gasoline policy memoranda
subfiles.about: Confidentially transmits memoranda on conserving technical information used to produce high-quality aviation gasoline.
subfiles.summary: The instruction provides the Tokyo Ambassador with confidential information about the Government's decision on aviation-gasoline technology. It lists two enclosed memoranda, dated December 18 and December 21, concerning conservation of the relevant technical information.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of conversation with James A. Moffett
subfiles.about: Records James A. Moffett's inquiry about the moral embargo on petroleum technology for Japanese and Soviet interests.
subfiles.summary: Moffett asked about reports that the Department was restricting technical information and aviation-gasoline refining machinery for the Manchurian Oil Monopoly. After consulting Green, the Department confirmed that American oil companies had been asked to withhold further plans and technical information from Japanese and Soviet interests. Moffett endorsed the policy but expressed concern that he had first heard of the meeting through the president of a non-American oil company.

subfiles.title: Universal Oil Products request concerning Manchukuo work and George E. Shelton
subfiles.from: H. J. Halle, Universal Oil Products Company
subfiles.about: Requests guidance on ordinary-gasoline facilities in Manchukuo and Embassy contact with company engineer George E. Shelton.
subfiles.summary: Halle says the company informed Japan Gasoline Company president Saneyoshi that it was ending further information and services relating to high-quality aviation gasoline and was also withholding information on other processes. He asks whether the company may continue providing plans and help for ordinary-gasoline cracking plants in Manchukuo under its 1928 contract. He also supplies George E. Shelton's Yokohama and Kawasaki addresses and asks that the Tokyo Ambassador be told about the engineer.

subfiles.title: Reply to H. J. Halle concerning Japan Gasoline Company contracts
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Halle's letter and says most questions were handled by telephone while the Embassy request remained under consideration.
subfiles.summary: Green refers to the December 20 letter and the contracts between Universal Oil Products Company and Japan Gasoline Company. He says that all but one of the issues were dealt with in their December 21 telephone conversation and that the request for a telegram to the Tokyo Ambassador was still being considered.

subfiles.title: Universal Oil Products acknowledgment of the Department's December 19 instructions
subfiles.from: H. J. Halle, Universal Oil Products Company
subfiles.about: Formally acknowledges the Department's December 19 letter and promises copies of affected contracts.
subfiles.summary: Halle acknowledges receipt of the December 19 letter written on behalf of the Secretary of State and its enclosure. He promises to prepare and send copies of the existing contracts involving the parties affected by the Department's instructions.

subfiles.title: Universal Oil Products letter and telegram authorizing Kenneth Jones to proceed to Germany
subfiles.from: S. R. Wilson, Universal Oil Products Company
subfiles.about: Reports that engineer Kenneth Jones was instructed to resume his journey to Germany after temporarily remaining in Genoa.
subfiles.summary: Wilson explains that Jones was traveling to Germany to help place two non-selective polymerization units into operation for motor-gasoline polymer production. As a precaution following the December 14 meeting, the company had told him to wait in Genoa, but after discussions with the Department it cabled him to proceed as originally planned. The enclosed telegram records that instruction.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Universal Oil Products' letter about Kenneth Jones
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the company's letter and copy of its telegram to Kenneth Jones.
subfiles.summary: Green confirms receipt of Universal Oil Products Company's December 20 letter. He identifies Jones's assignment as assisting with two non-selective polymerization units in Germany.

subfiles.title: M. W. Kellogg Company letter concerning Stone and Webster cooperation
subfiles.from: F. E. Johnson Jr., M. W. Kellogg Company
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Green / Department of State
subfiles.about: Reports a conversation with Stone and Webster president Muhlfeld concerning cooperation with the Department's aviation-gasoline policy.
subfiles.summary: The OCR of the body is badly damaged, but the surviving text and the Department's reply identify the subject as technical information for producing high-quality aviation gasoline. The letter conveyed Stone and Webster's cooperative attitude toward carrying out the Government's policy.

subfiles.title: Department acknowledgment to the M. W. Kellogg Company
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Thanks the company for reporting Stone and Webster's position on restricted aviation-gasoline information.
subfiles.summary: Green acknowledges the December 21 letter about the company's conversation with Stone and Webster president Muhlfeld. He asks that the Department's appreciation be conveyed to Muhlfeld for his attitude concerning technical information for high-quality aviation gasoline.

subfiles.title: Pan American report on gasoline blending agents
subfiles.from: Robert E. Wilson, Pan American Petroleum & Transport Company
subfiles.about: Reports that the company neither manufactured nor sold the four blending agents named by the Department.
subfiles.summary: Wilson states that the company did not manufacture or sell tetraethyl lead, iso-octane, neo-hexane, or alkylates and did not expect to do so within a year. It therefore would not submit current export reports but would remember the Department's request if future sales to Japan or the Soviet Union became possible.

subfiles.title: Transfer sheet for moral-embargo correspondence
subfiles.about: Records the transfer of document 894.24/774 to the moral-embargo file.
subfiles.summary: The sheet contains no substantive correspondence. It directs researchers to file 700.00116 Moral Embargo/15 for document 894.24/774.

subfiles.title: Atlantic Refining Company report of no blending-agent shipments
subfiles.from: V. L. Elliott, Atlantic Refining Company
subfiles.about: Reports that Atlantic Refining made no shipments of the specified gasoline blending agents to the countries named by the Department.
subfiles.summary: The company says it shipped no gasoline blending agents or related products to the countries identified in Green's December 19 letter. It adds that it did not produce or sell the named blending agents separately from automobile fuel.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Atlantic Refining's export report
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Atlantic Refining's statement that it exported no relevant blending agents.
subfiles.summary: Green thanks Elliott for the company's December 26 response. He restates that Atlantic Refining had not exported gasoline blending agents or related products to the countries named in the Department's inquiry.

subfiles.title: Texas Company report of no 1939 blending-agent exports
subfiles.about: Reports that the Texas Company exported no gasoline blending agents to Japan or the Soviet Union during 1939.
subfiles.summary: Saunders answers the Department's inquiry about tetraethyl lead, iso-octane, neo-hexane, and alkylates. He states that the company made no such exports to Japan or the Soviet Union during 1939, contemplated no sales at present, and would report any change.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of the Texas Company's export report
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Texas Company's report that it exported no specified blending agents in 1939.
subfiles.summary: Green thanks Saunders for the December 26 letter. He repeats that the company made no 1939 exports of tetraethyl lead, iso-octane, neo-hexane, or alkylates to Japan or the Soviet Union.

subfiles.title: Phillips Petroleum report on 1939 sales and 1940 Japanese contracts
subfiles.from: K. S. Adams, Phillips Petroleum Company
subfiles.to: Secretary of State, attention Joseph C. Green
subfiles.about: Reports Phillips Petroleum's blending-agent deliveries for export to Japan, its lack of Soviet business, and its substantial 1940 Japanese contracts.
subfiles.summary: Adams reports no sales or contracts of any kind with the Soviet Union. For export to Japan through Mitsui & Co. in San Francisco, Phillips delivered two drums of tetraethyl lead, 51,170 of commercial iso-octane, and 12,372 of products occurring naturally in petroleum, as transcribed in the letter. He says substantial Japanese contracts remained for 1940 and proposes semiannual reports. Adams also argues that the profitable sales justified new production facilities that would strengthen the company's ability to meet U.S. government needs during a national emergency.

subfiles.title: Department request for monthly Phillips Petroleum shipment reports
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Green, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Phillips Petroleum's report and asks for monthly reports on contracted 1940 shipments to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Green thanks Adams for the information about 1939 sales and deliveries for export to Japan and the Soviet Union. Because Phillips had contracts for 1940 Japanese deliveries, he asks the company to submit monthly shipment reports if convenient.

subfiles.title: Letter transmitting the December 20 aviation-gasoline press statement to H. J. Halle
subfiles.about: Sends Halle two copies of the Department's December 20 press statement on aviation-gasoline technology.
subfiles.summary: Green responds to Halle's oral request by enclosing two copies of the press release. The statement concerns delivery to certain countries of technical information required to produce high-quality aviation gasoline.

subfiles.title: Letter to C. S. Reed transmitting the press statement and proposed Machino Import telegram
subfiles.about: Sends the Lummus Company copies of the aviation-gasoline press statement and a suggested telegram to Machino Import.
subfiles.summary: Green refers to recent conversations that Reed and Nathaniel Ely had with the Division of Controls about supplying certain countries with technical information for high-quality aviation gasoline. He encloses two copies of the Department's December 20 press statement and the text of a proposed telegram to Machino Import previously given to Ely.
